AreaLineStyle.description:
Stroke/halo/labels for an area chart's top-edge line and value labels.

Vega-Lite itself compiles an area's edge line as a genuine separate
``line`` mark (``mark: {type: area, line: {...}}`` produces independent
``area``/``line`` marks in the compiled Vega spec), and dbt charts'
emitter builds the same separate line mark by hand. So the edge's
stroke geometry belongs here, on the "line" identity — not on
``AreaMarkStyle`` (fill only).

Curve is a single shared value driving both the fill AND this edge line
(they trace one silhouette) and lives solely on ``AreaMarkStyle.curve``;
``connect`` has no area equivalent (see ``AreaMarkStyle``'s docstring).
A second, differently-scoped ``curve`` field here would silently do
nothing — the exact bug this type was split out to prevent.

labels.description: Value label style for the area's plotted points; inherits from global.

AxisLabelOverlapConfig.description:
Two-bool overlap strategy enablement for x-axis labels.

Each bool enables (True) or disables (False) a strategy step.
None means "not authored — inherit from the theme cascade."
The resolver applies enabled strategies in fixed order: skip → tilt.
On bucketed temporal axes, skip advances label visibility by one meaningful
calendar period while preserving the encoding and label format time units.
Other temporal axes use parity skip. Categorical axes never skip because
removing a category label loses domain information; they only tilt.

Attributes:
    tilt: Walk tilt_increments and apply the first angle that fits.
    skip: Thin temporal labels; ignored on categorical axes.

Example YAML:
    overlap:
      tilt: true
      skip: true

skip.description: Enable temporal label thinning; ignored on categorical axes; None inherits from parent axis.

tilt.description: Enable label tilt strategy; None inherits from parent axis.

AxisLabelStyle.description:

This is the universal base — fields that are meaningful on both dimension
and measure axes. Dimension-only fields (tilt_increments, values,

expr stays here: it is universal and read by time_unit_detect.py on both
axes.

align.description: Horizontal text alignment of labels. 'left'/'right'/'center' are absolute. 'inward' hugs the plot (own-side: left on a left axis, right on a right axis); 'outward' hugs away from the plot (Vega-Lite's default growth direction). inward/outward are a no-op on an axis with no left/right edge. 'auto' uses Vega-Lite's default, except that a right-edge quantitative axis with a number format and a tabular label font decimal-aligns its labels; a house format alias does so even over an align set here.

angle.description: Label rotation angle in degrees; 'auto' uses Vega-Lite's default.

bound.description: Hide labels that overflow the axis range; 'auto' uses Vega-Lite's default.

expr.description: Custom Vega expression for label text; None uses smart temporal defaults when applicable.

flush.description: Align first/last label flush with the scale range; 'auto' uses Vega-Lite's default.

format.description: Tick value format string; None uses auto-format.

max_width.description: Maximum label width in pixels; 'auto' uses Vega-Lite's default (180px).

min_gap.description: Minimum pixel gap between labels; None uses Vega-Lite's default (0px).

offset.description: Pixel offset of the label from its tick anchor; 'auto' uses Vega-Lite's default.

overlap.description: Label overlap strategy enablement. None inherits from the theme cascade. Set individual bools to enable/disable; they are applied in fixed order skip→tilt. padding.description: Padding between axis labels and ticks in pixels; None inherits from parent axis.

visible.description: Show axis labels; 'auto' uses Vega-Lite's default (labels shown).

AxisTicksStyle.description:
Tick marks on an axis: visibility, color, size, and cadence.

Every axis slot uses this shape except axis_x, which adds ticks.time_unit
for calendar cadence. Which cadence fields actually apply depends on the
axis: see the count and step descriptions below.

color.description: Tick color; None uses Vega-Lite's default.

count.description: Target number of axis ticks, or 'auto' for the engine's own sparse ladder: a target everywhere, never an exact count. On the measure axis (axis_y) the renderer computes an explicit round-numbered ladder of at most this many ticks. On axis_x it passes through as VL's axis.tickCount: a temporal scale honors it closely, a quantitative one rounds to a nearby round-numbered ladder. To name the interval instead of the count, author ticks.step on a quantitative axis_x. An ordinal axis_x has no tick-count concept and ignores this.

length.description: Tick length in pixels; None uses Vega-Lite's default.

offset.description: Pixel offset of ticks from their default position; 'auto' means no offset.

step.description: Tick interval on axis_x. Alongside ticks.time_unit it is a multiple of that calendar grain (time_unit: year, step: 5 -> a tick every 5 years). On its own it is a numeric interval for a quantitative axis (step: 1000 -> a tick every 1000), and acts as a floor rather than a fixed ladder, so the axis keeps covering the data as its range grows. A bare step on an axis that is not quantitative is an error, not a no-op; axis_y rejects step entirely (set ticks.count there instead).

visible.description: Show axis ticks; None inherits from parent axis.

width.description: Tick stroke width in pixels; None uses Vega-Lite's default.

Board.description:
Compiled board ready for execution and rendering.

Stage: COMPILE output / EXECUTE and RENDER input

This is the main output of compilation. It contains:
- Resolved definitions (variables, queries, charts)
- Unified layout structure
- Calculated dimensions
- Applied defaults and metadata

Guarantees:

    - title: Always set (empty string if not provided)
    - layout: Always present (unified structure)
    - All charts resolved to Chart objects
    - All queries resolved to query objects

DimensionTicksStyle.description:
axis_x-only: adds the calendar unit that anchors a step cadence.

Distinct from ``DimensionLabelStyle.time_unit`` (label-cadence override)
and ``AxisXStyle.time_unit`` (bucketing grain) — three different
time_unit fields, three different meanings.

On axis_x it passes through as VL's axis.tickCount: a temporal scale honors it closely, a quantitative one rounds to a nearby round-numbered ladder. On its own it is a numeric interval for a quantitative axis (step: 1000 -> a tick every 1000), and acts as a floor rather than a fixed ladder, so the axis keeps covering the data as its range grows. A bare step on an axis that is not quantitative is an error, not a no-op; axis_y rejects step entirely (set ticks.count there instead).

visible.description: Show axis ticks. "auto" shows the tick only where the gridlines can't reach all the way to the labels on their own; None inherits from parent axis.

To name the interval instead of the count, author ticks.step on a quantitative axis_x. An ordinal axis_x has no tick-count concept and ignores this.

On its own it is a numeric interval for a quantitative axis (step: 1000 -> a tick every 1000), and acts as a floor rather than a fixed ladder, so the axis keeps covering the data as its range grows. A bare step on an axis that is not quantitative is an error, not a no-op; axis_y rejects step entirely (set ticks.count there instead).

Whether a chart visually answers "what am I pointing at", beyond the tooltip.

Hovering a mark recedes the others so the one under the cursor stands out.

line, area, and scatter instead draw a datum marker plus a drop line down
to the axis, since receding a stroke reads as an interruption rather than
emphasis. A family that does not yet answer the question ignores the
switch rather than half-answering it. Named for what it does rather than
for the trigger, which would read as gating the tooltip beside it (it
does not).

The line/area drop line's color and width: each theme picks a neutral one
scaffold rung past its own measure gridline, at twice that gridline's
width, so the line reads as structure rather than as another data series.

The browser runtime reads `visible` and `recede_contrast`, and the engine
reads the same pair to bake the receded look of a mark a board variable
does not select, so changing either changes the rendered SVG of a board
that holds one. The drop line's paint stays runtime-only.

A single item in a layout.

Represents either a chart or a nested board in the layout.

MultiplesConfig.description:
Small-multiples partition, keyed by layout direction.

``rows`` stacks one panel per value vertically; ``columns`` lays them out
side by side. Both are optional and either or both may be set — rows-only is
a row stack, columns-only a horizontal strip, both a grid — but at least one
is required. Naming the direction makes the authored surface self-describing
(no positional list to document) and lets a single dimension pick its axis.

columns.description: Column whose distinct values become side-by-side panel columns.

rows.description: Column whose distinct values become vertically stacked panel rows.

scale.description: Measure-scale sharing across panels. 'shared' (default) makes panels visually comparable; 'independent' gives each panel its own scale.

NoteAnnotation.description:
Text at a point, or pinned to the plot frame when it has no anchor.

With `min()` or `max()` on one axis and the other omitted, the note sits at
the row holding that extreme.

connector.description: Draws a line, or a line ending in an arrowhead, from the anchor to text moved away with dx/dy. Unset draws none.

plane.description: Draw below the data marks, or above them.

series.description: Which series a computed anchor or trend is computed for. `total` pools every series' rows, or takes the per-x sum on a stacked chart.

style.description: Appearance overrides for this annotation's marks.

text.description: Text drawn with the annotation; `{{ value | format }}` prints the anchor.

x.description: Where on the x axis. `min()` or `max()` with y omitted anchors at the row holding that x extreme.

y.description: Where on the y axis. `min()` or `max()` with x omitted anchors at the row holding that y extreme.

y_column.description: The y column the annotation refers to: it picks the y axis that plots the column, and the rows a computed y anchor or trend reads. Required for a computed y anchor, trend or derived note on a chart with several y columns or `layers:`.

line.description: The connector from the anchor to the text.

text.description: The note's text.

frame.description: Defaults for a note pinned to the plot frame.

text.description: Text of a note with no anchor.

position.description: Where a note with no anchor sits on the plot frame.

curve.description: Line interpolation: `linear` is straight, `natural` bends a note's connector and smooths a trend's curve.

length.description: Distance between the anchor and the note's text when a connector is drawn, in pixels.

align.description: Position along the edge; `auto` is center, or another spot when that one is taken.

edge.description: Side of the anchor the text sits on; `auto` is past the value: top on a vertical chart, right on a horizontal one.

overlay.description: True draws the text over the plot; False reserves room for it.

padding.description: Space between the note's text and the box drawn around it, in pixels.

dy.description: Vertical nudge after placement, in pixels.

halo.description: Width of the canvas-colored outline behind the text, in pixels; 0 draws none. `auto` draws a 3px outline only on text that overlaps a bar, point or area fill.

halo_opacity.description: Opacity of the halo as a whole, 0 to 1; overlapping letter outlines do not darken.

max_width.description: Width in pixels a note with no anchor wraps its text to; `auto` is a readable measure of about 28 characters, kept inside the plot. A note anchored at a point does not wrap.

position.description: Which side of the anchor the text sits on, and where along it.

analytic.description: The extra-short thousand, million, billion and trillion suffixes, where a magnitude is declared once (en-US: K, M, B, T). A leading space, where a locale wants one, is part of the suffix.

currency.description: The currency prefix and suffix (e.g. `["$", ""]`) a `$` in a d3 spec prints.

grouping.description: The group sizes (e.g. `[3]`), cycled as needed.

Controls client-side row paging for table charts. This is a presentation
concern (how many rows to show per page), distinct from query-level ``limit``
which controls how many rows are *fetched*.

style model:

- ``pagination: true``  → PaginationConfig(enabled=True)
- ``pagination: false`` → PaginationConfig(enabled=False)

SchemaQuery.description:
Query the LayeredSchemaResolver in-process.

Dispatches to list_sources / list_schemas / list_tables / profile_table /
profile_column based on which optional fields are populated:
- (no source) → list_sources (returns configured source names)
- source only → list_schemas(source)
- source + schema → list_tables(source, schema)
- source + schema + table → profile_table(source, schema, table) → column rows
- source + schema + table + column → profile_column(source, schema, table, column)

Note: The YAML field is ``schema`` but the Python attribute is ``schema_name``
to avoid shadowing ``BaseModel.schema`` (a Pydantic v2 legacy classmethod).

Fields must be literal strings — Jinja templates (``{{``, ``{%``, ``{#``)
are rejected at model construction time.  Field prerequisites are also
validated at construction time: ``table`` requires ``schema``; ``column``
requires both ``schema`` and ``table``.

the chart's resolved ``axis_y.orient`` — there is no authorable

ValuesQuery.description:
Inline data query with rows embedded directly in the YAML.

Provides two syntaxes:
1. Dict rows (verbose): rows: [{month: "Jan", revenue: 100}, ...]
2. Columns + values (compact, SQL-style): columns: [month, revenue], values: [["Jan", 100], ...]

When using columns + values, rows are computed automatically via model_post_init.

Example (dict rows):
    >>> query = ValuesQuery(rows=[{"month": "Jan", "revenue": 100}])

Example (columns + values):
    >>> query = ValuesQuery(
    ...     columns=["month", "revenue"],
    ...     values=[["Jan", 100], ["Feb", 140]],
    ... )
    >>> query.rows  # [{"month": "Jan", "revenue": 100}, {"month": "Feb", "revenue": 140}]
